Student’s Book p.7 · Exercise 7 · Listening 1.9

A successful person

Listen once for the main idea. Then listen again and complete the details.

Roadmap SB · Track 1.9
Show the audio script

Alex: Actually, a person who I think is really successful is my grandma, Elizabeth. My mum’s mum.

Marian: That’s lovely! Why’s that, then?

Alex: Well, she’s not famous or rich, but she’s a really nice and happy person. She’s retired now, but she’s still very active – even at 85! She always gets up between five and six in the morning and cleans the house. After breakfast, she usually goes out for a long walk. She walks everywhere, actually – she hardly ever uses public transport.

Marian: She sounds great! Tell me more …

Alex: OK, so, every Wednesday she looks after my kids – her great-grandchildren – all day. They’re three and four, and very energetic! She was a teacher in a primary school, so she’s very good with children. She plays with them all the time.

Marian: Wow! To be like that at 85, that’s amazing!

Supported speaking

Two short answers

Each question has its own starter and example.

42. Imagine you have a quiet evening. What would you choose: a mystery, an adventure film or a self-help book? Why?

Start: I’d choose … because I enjoy …
I’d choose a mystery because I enjoy trying to imagine what happens next. I usually watch films with subtitles.

43. Imagine you want to grow something useful at home. What would you grow and how would you use it?

Start: I’d like to grow … . I could use it …
I’d like to grow basil and rocket. I could use them in simple salads instead of buying herbs every time.
